recognize_zh: 老年病人背部、雙上肢到臀部的皮膚呈瀰漫性、融合的鮮紅色紅皮症（erythroderma），幾乎無正常皮膚間隔，皮膚鬆弛有細紋，這種全身紅皮症是 Sézary 症候群的典型臨床表現。
features: Clinical photograph of the posterior trunk, arms and buttocks of an elderly patient
Diffuse, confluent bright red to violaceous erythema involving nearly the entire visible body surface (>80% BSA)
No discrete patches, plaques or tumors; the erythema is uniform with little spared skin
Skin appears thin and finely wrinkled with fine scaling over the lower back
Relative accentuation of color in skin folds and dependent areas
describe_en: Clinical photograph shows an elderly patient with generalized, confluent erythema involving the back, both arms and the buttocks, with virtually no uninvolved skin. The skin is diffusely red with fine scaling and wrinkling, and there are no discrete plaques, tumors or ulceration. Palmoplantar keratoderma, lymphadenopathy and alopecia cannot be assessed in this view. Erythroderma is nonspecific; in conjunction with a clonal circulating T-cell population (Sézary count ≥1000/µL, or CD4:CD8 ≥10, or loss of CD7/CD26), findings are consistent with Sézary syndrome.

ddx.vs: Erythrodermic MF has the same skin appearance but lacks the B2 level of blood involvement required for Sézary syndrome.
Eczematous erythroderma has polyclonal T cells, spongiosis on biopsy and a history of atopy, without a circulating CD4+CD26− clone.
Psoriatic erythroderma shows a history of psoriatic plaques, nail pitting and psoriasiform hyperplasia with parakeratosis and neutrophils in the stratum corneum.
Drug erythroderma follows medication exposure with facial edema, eosinophilia and organ involvement, and resolves on drug withdrawal.
